==Problem==

Which of the following numbers is not a perfect square?

<math>\textbf{(A) }1^{2016}\qquad\textbf{(B) }2^{2017}\qquad\textbf{(C) }3^{2018}\qquad\textbf{(D) }4^{2019}\qquad \textbf{(E) }5^{2020}</math>

==Solution 1==
Our answer must have an odd exponent in order for it to not be a square.  Because <imath>4</imath> is a perfect square, <imath>4^{2019}</imath> is also a perfect square, so our answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }2^{2017}}</imath>.
==Solution 2 (more detailed explanation of Solution 1)==
Any even integer <imath>m</imath> can be divided into <imath>2n</imath> where <imath>n</imath> is an integer as well. Therefore, <imath>\textbf{(A), (C),}</imath> and <imath>\textbf{(E)}</imath> are immediately disqualified, as when <imath>m</imath> is even, <imath>a^m</imath> can always be written as <imath>(a^\frac{m}{2})^2</imath> as <imath>(a^m)^n = a^{mn}</imath> and vice versa. Only odd exponents are non-squares, therefore. <imath>4=2^2</imath>, which means <imath>4^{2019}=(2^2)^2019=(2^{2019})^2</imath> by the <imath>(a^m)^n = a^{mn}</imath> rule. The only option left is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }2^{2017}}</imath>.
